title: Evaluation metrics: correctness, format, tone and safety

videos.script: A test set gives you a number. This lesson asks which number. {{title}} Start with correctness. The prompt sorts fifty-six of seventy messages correctly. That sentence hides where the other fourteen went. A confusion matrix shows every one of them, label against label. {{matrix}} From it you read precision and recall. You also find six urgent messages filed as normal. One of them is a card charged for an order nobody placed. {{urgent}} Format is counted apart, so a code fence never looks like a wrong opinion. {{format}} Then tone. Twelve replies meet a handful of rules: exclamation marks, length, phrases the shop never uses, promises it cannot keep. The rules catch what they name. They also flag one sentence that is perfectly fine. {{tone}} Last, two prompts with exactly the same accuracy. One of them sends nine messages to billing that do not belong there. {{many}} By the end you report metrics side by side, and you know which mistakes cost the most. {{close}}
